title: Improper Authentication
summary: Authentication logic mistakenly treats a nonzero strcmp() result as success.

title: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input
summary: Unbounded %s input can copy more data than the destination buffer can hold.

title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
summary: An unchecked copy can overwrite memory beyond a fixed-size stack buffer.

title: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
summary: A fixed-size heap allocation is followed by an unbounded copy.

title: Out-of-bounds Read
summary: The index is used without checking whether it is inside the array bounds.

title: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
summary: User-controlled text is interpreted as a printf format string.

title: Improper Null Termination
summary: strncpy() may fill the destination without appending a null terminator.

title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
summary: Unsigned arithmetic is performed without checking whether the result wraps.

title: Integer Underflow or Wraparound
summary: Subtracting a larger unsigned value from a smaller one can wrap to a huge value.

title: Off-by-one Error
summary: The <= condition writes one byte past the end of the array.

title: Unchecked Return Value
summary: The code uses fopen() results without checking whether the call succeeded.

title: Divide By Zero
summary: Invalid input can make the divisor zero.

title: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
summary: Allocated memory is not released after it is no longer needed.

title: Double Free
summary: The same heap allocation is released twice.

title: Use After Free
summary: The program accesses heap memory after that allocation has been freed.

title: Use of Uninitialized Variable
summary: A security decision depends on a variable that is not initialized on every path.

title: Use of sizeof() on a Pointer Type
summary: sizeof(buf) returns the size of the pointer, not the allocated object.

title: NULL Pointer Dereference
summary: strchr() can return NULL, which is dereferenced without validation.

title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
summary: Untrusted input directly controls an allocation size without an upper bound.

title: Out-of-bounds Write
summary: An unchecked index controls where a write occurs relative to a fixed-size array.
